title: Smooth general member of an immersive linear system
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $Y$ a scheme smooth over $k$, $\mathcal L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module, $V$ a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space and $\psi:V\to\Gamma(Y,\mathcal L)$ a $k$-linear map. Assume that the image of $\psi$ generates $\mathcal L$ and that the associated morphism $Y\to\mathbf P(V)$ is an immersion. Then for general $v\in V\otimes_kk'$ the scheme $H_v$ is smooth over $k'$.
Here, for a $k$-vector space $V$ of dimension $r$ with a basis $v_1,\dots,v_r$, a property $P$ *holds for general* $v$ if there is a nonempty Zariski open $U\subseteq\mathbf A^r_k$ such that $P(v)$ holds for every field extension $k'/k$ and every $v=\sum_i a_iv_i\in V\otimes_kk'$ with $(a_1,\dots,a_r)\in U(k')$; and $H_v=Z(\psi(v))\subseteq Y_{k'}$ is the zero scheme of the section $\psi(v)=\sum_ia_i\psi(v_i)$ of $\mathcal L|_{Y_{k'}}$.
The scheme, smoothness, immersion, invertible-sheaf, generation, zero-scheme and base-change notions are those of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], [def-sc-invertible-module], [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections], [def-pc-zero-scheme] and [def-pc-base-change].

source.place: Tag 0FD6, lemma-bertini (in Situation 0FD3, situation-family-divisors, varieties.tex lines 10910-10964)

proof.text: Reindex the finite basis by ULift(Fin r), with r its cardinality. Generation is unchanged because the ranges of the stalk germs are unchanged under a bijection. Trivialize the invertible sheaf on the complements of the zero loci of its generating sections; the stalk-span criterion and the local-ring maximal-ideal argument show that these opens cover. On these opens the native projective morphism equals the morphism specified by the generating sections, by the uniqueness statement of the projective-space functor of points. Coordinate ratios show that reindexing this morphism is its composite with the projective coordinate reindexing isomorphism. Thus the reindexed morphism is still an immersion. These comparisons do not require a nonempty indexing set.

source.place: Situation 0FD3, choice of a finite basis; Lemma 0FD6, associated projective immersion

proof.text: Choose a basis of $V$ and form the universal section $s_{\mathrm{univ}}=\sum_i x_i\psi(v_i)$ on $\mathbf A^r_k\times_kY$; by the definition of the zero-scheme construction and base change, its zero scheme $H_{\mathrm{univ}}$ has fibre over every coefficient point $v$ equal to $H_v=Z(\psi(v))$. In Lean, compare tensorPullback with the ordinary module pullback by uniqueness of left adjoints. The adjunction units identify the sections, and the composition isomorphism sends the iterated unit to the composite unit. Pulling back the universal sum therefore evaluates its coordinates at the coefficient tuple. Zero-locus invariance under module isomorphisms and the ideal-sheaf comap pullback square give the required cartesian square, for arbitrary field extensions.

source.place: Situation 0FD3, construction of the universal divisor

proof.text: Let $\Sigma$ be the non-smooth locus of the projection $q:H_{\mathrm{univ}}\to\mathbf A^r_k$. The dimension estimate in [lem-zl-bertini-singular-locus-dimension] (Stacks Tag 0FD6) gives $\dim(\Sigma)<r$ and a proper closed subset $B\subsetneq\mathbf A^r_k$ containing $q(\Sigma)$.

Put $U=\mathbf A^r_k\setminus B$, an open subset. Since $q(\Sigma)\subseteq B$, every point of the open $q^{-1}(U)$ has an open neighbourhood on which $q$ is smooth; these neighbourhoods intersected with $q^{-1}(U)$ cover $q^{-1}(U)$, so $q_U:q^{-1}(U)\to U$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source]. For a field extension $k'/k$ and $v\in U(k')$, viewed as $\operatorname{Spec}k'\to U\subseteq\mathbf A^r_k$, the fibre $H_{\mathrm{univ}}\times_{\mathbf A^r_k}\operatorname{Spec}k'=q^{-1}(U)\times_U\operatorname{Spec}k'$ is the base change of $q_U$, hence smooth over $k'$ by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2); by Step 2 it is $H_v$.

source.place: Tag 0FD6, conclusion after the dimension estimate

proof.text: Because $B$ is proper, $U$ is nonempty and Zariski open. The same $U$ works after every field extension by the universal-family base-change identification in Step 2, which is exactly the stated meaning of 'for general' $v$. Finally transport the open back along Spec of the polynomial-variable renaming isomorphism. Evaluation commutes with renaming, and the finite sum defining the member section is unchanged by the indexing equivalence.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0FD6, lemma-bertini proof via the universal divisor and singular-locus dimension estimate; explicit adjunction-unit and coordinate-reindexing comparisons supplied in Lean by E5

lean.note: An arbitrary finite basis indexes the affine coefficient space. The k-linear map is an additive map to top-open sections with its canonical scalar law written explicitly; general means a single nonempty open that works for every extension field. Helpers construct its actual coefficient point, pulled-back section and compatible global-section family.
